elements.text: Good morning, Roosevelt! Only 17 days until your exam on Nov 9.
Topic: IPv4 Address Model & Network/Host Portions

segments.speech: Good morning, Roosevelt! It's Friday morning, October 23, and we have 17 days left before your big exam on November 9th. Let's start fresh and energetic! Today we are tackling the IPv4 Address Model and breaking down network and host portions. Does that sound good?

elements.text: An IPv4 address is a unique 32-bit numerical label assigned to every device connected to a computer network.
Like a mailing address for your computer!

segments.speech: Think of an IP address like a physical house address. If you want to send a letter to a friend, you need their street name and house number. On the internet, devices use an IPv4 address to find each other. An IPv4 address is made up of 32 bits. Let's look at how this is structured on the board. Make sense so far?

elements.text: An IPv4 address is split into two main parts: the Network portion and the Host portion.
Network ID: Identifies the specific street or building
Host ID: Identifies the exact room or computer

segments.speech: Every IPv4 address is actually split into two parts: the network portion, which tells us the general neighborhood, and the host portion, which tells us the exact device. Does that division make sense so far, Roosevelt?
